prompt: Add a wrapText(text, width) function to textkit that breaks text into lines no longer than width, splitting on spaces; a single word longer than width stays alone on its own line. It returns an array of lines. Put it in src/wrap.js, export it from the package entry point, add tests in test/wrap.test.js, document it in the README, then review your own change and write what you would flag in review to review-notes.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const w=require("./src").wrapText;const j=JSON.stringify;const ok=typeof w==="function"&&j(w("the quick brown fox",10))===j(["the quick","brown fox"])&&j(w("a extraordinarily b",5))===j(["a","extraordinarily","b"])&&j(w("",10))==="[]";process.exit(ok?0:1)'
node -e 'const w=require("./src").wrapText;const j=JSON.stringify;process.exit(j(w("abc def",7))===j(["abc def"])&&j(w("abc def",3))===j(["abc","def"])?0:1)'

c=0; for p in 'whitespace|newline|tab|space' 'width.{0,12}(0|zero|negative|less)|non.?positive' 'long(er)? word|overflow|exceed' 'null|undefined|non.?string|not a string|type'; do cat review-notes.md 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE "$p" && c=$((c+1)); done; [ "$c" -ge 2 ]

rubric.criterion: wrapText in src/wrap.js is exported from src/index.js, wraps greedily, returns an array, and no line exceeds width unless it is a single longer word.
test/wrap.test.js covers a normal wrap, a word longer than width, an empty string and a line exactly equal to width, and passes.
README documents the signature and shows an example whose output is correct.
review-notes.md gives specific, true observations tied to the code, such as handling of repeated spaces or newlines, width of 0 or less, or the long-word policy.
The final message reports the test run result.
